title: DNS + Edge Routing Plan (Controlled Failover Tests) — records, TTLs, rollback, change windows
content:
Doc intent
- This is the infra planning “sheet” for DNS + edge routing changes used during controlled failover tests (staging first, then prod low-risk slice).
- Audience: Infra/Networking + SRE + Release Eng.
- Scope: public ingress (API/streaming), internal edge-to-region routing entrypoints, and the TTL/change-window/rollback plan.

Owner / approvals
- Infra owner: Victor Alvarez (Network routing/DNS)
- Approvers for production windows: Irene Choi (Dir Infra Eng), Connor O’Brien (Release Eng), Rafael Mendes (SRE delivery)
- Input: Emily Zhao (cross-region connectivity), Harish Reddy (capacity ops)

Assumptions / current architecture (as of 2025-04)
- Public traffic enters via Edge (Cloudflare) and is forwarded to regional ingress (Envoy/NLB) per routing policy.
- DNS is primarily for:
  1) Edge hostname(s) (stable) and
  2) Regional origin hostnames (not directly customer-facing, but used by Edge origin pools / health checks)
- We are NOT moving customers directly between regional A records; failover is primarily an Edge/orchestrator action. DNS knobs are used for:
  - conservative safety fallback (last resort)
  - health-check / origin selection behavior
  - shortening TTLs pre-game-day so that emergency DNS-based mitigations are viable if needed

Environments + terminology
- Regions (primary):
  - use1 = us-east-1 (Ashburn)
  - usw2 = us-west-2 (Oregon)
  - euw1 = eu-west-1 (Dublin)
  - aps1 = ap-southeast-1 (Singapore)
- Edge POP routing: handled by Cloudflare (steering via origin pool health + header-based policies from orchestrator)
- Controlled failover types:
  - “Edge policy failover”: move a scoped %/tier/route from region A → region B
  - “Origin pool health failover”: mark origin unhealthy to force pool selection
  - “DNS emergency switch”: change DNS to point Edge hostname to alternate edge entrypoint (rare)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TABLE A — Customer-facing edge hostnames (stable) + TTL strategy

| Hostname | Env | Provider | Record type | Current target | TTL (current) | TTL (pre-test) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| api.redwoodinference.com | prod | Cloudflare DNS | CNAME | api-edge.prod.redwoodinfra.net | 300s | 60s | Primary API. We do NOT plan to flip this for tests; TTL reduction is to keep the “DNS emergency switch” feasible. |
| stream.redwoodinference.com | prod | Cloudflare DNS | CNAME | stream-edge.prod.redwoodinfra.net | 300s | 60s | Streaming is most sensitive to mid-connection routing changes; tests should avoid DNS flips. |
| api.staging.redwoodinference.com | staging | Cloudflare DNS | CNAME | api-edge.staging.redwoodinfra.net | 300s | 60s | TTL can be reduced more aggressively in staging if needed (even 30s) but keep consistent with prod to reduce surprises. |
| stream.staging.redwoodinference.com | staging | Cloudflare DNS | CNAME | stream-edge.staging.redwoodinfra.net | 300s | 60s | Ensure websocket/HTTP2 settings match prod. |

TTL notes
- Why 60s: below this we see diminishing returns vs caching behavior in some resolvers; also increases query volume.
- Keep TTL=60s only during “test window + 2h buffer”; revert to 300s same day.
- Rule: TTL reductions must be applied >=24h before prod test window to let caches converge (we can’t force all resolvers to pick up the shorter TTL instantly).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TABLE B — Regional origin hostnames (Edge → Region) and mapping

| Origin hostname | Env | Region | Backend type | Provider | Record type | Target | Health check | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| api-origin.use1.prod.redwoodinfra.net | prod | use1 | NLB | Route53 (private + CF origin) | A (alias) | nlb-api-use1-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-api-use1 | Used in Cloudflare origin pool “api-prod”. |
| api-origin.usw2.prod.redwoodinfra.net | prod | usw2 | NLB | Route53 | A (alias) | nlb-api-usw2-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-api-usw2 | Ensure target has headroom before shifting >25%. |
| api-origin.euw1.prod.redwoodinfra.net | prod | euw1 | NLB | Route53 | A (alias) | nlb-api-euw1-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-api-euw1 | Cross-region latency penalties; only fail over EU traffic to US if explicitly approved. |
| api-origin.aps1.prod.redwoodinfra.net | prod | aps1 | NLB | Route53 | A (alias) | nlb-api-aps1-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-api-aps1 | APAC capacity is currently bursty; avoid being the global failover target. |
| stream-origin.use1.prod.redwoodinfra.net | prod | use1 | NLB | Route53 | A (alias) | nlb-stream-use1-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-stream-use1 | Streaming health check should validate upgrade + steady bytes, not just 200 OK. |
| stream-origin.usw2.prod.redwoodinfra.net | prod | usw2 | NLB | Route53 | A (alias) | nlb-stream-usw2-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-stream-usw2 | |
| api-origin.use1.staging.redwoodinfra.net | staging | use1 | NLB | Route53 | A (alias) | nlb-api-use1-stg-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-api-use1-stg | Staging is where we validate HC false positives/negatives. |
| api-origin.usw2.staging.redwoodinfra.net | staging | usw2 | NLB | Route53 | A (alias) | nlb-api-usw2-stg-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com | cf-origin-hc-api-usw2-stg | |

Operational notes
- Origin hostname records are stable; the failover orchestrator should modify Cloudflare origin pool weights / steering policy (preferred), not DNS targets.
- “DNS emergency switch” means changing the *edge* CNAME target (Table A), not the regional origins.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TABLE C — Cloudflare origin pools + steering policy (summary for change review)

| Pool name | Hostname | Members | Default steering | Failover behavior | Change interface |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| api-prod | api.redwoodinference.com | use1/usw2/euw1/aps1 origins | geo-steer + policy headers | auto failover on member HC fail; can be overridden by orchestrator scoped rules | Cloudflare API via orchestrator (audited) |
| stream-prod | stream.redwoodinference.com | use1/usw2/euw1/aps1 origins | geo-steer + stickiness | failover more conservative; prefer degraded mode over aggressive mid-stream shift | Cloudflare API via orchestrator (audited) |
| api-staging | api.staging.redwoodinference.com | use1/usw2 origins | geo-steer | same | Cloudflare dashboard ok in staging (still log changes) |

Guardrails we want for controlled tests
- Ensure “origin health failover” isn’t triggered by synthetic probe noise (see Region Health Signals doc).
- For streaming: avoid any plan that flips active connections (expectation: new connections go to target; existing continue until completion when possible).
- Explicit stop condition: if elevated disconnects > X% for > Y min (SRE to fill in based on ENG-2850/2851).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TTL + caching gotchas (notes from prior incidents)
- Short TTL does not guarantee fast cutover:
  - Some resolvers ignore TTL floors or have prefetch behavior.
  - Mobile carrier resolvers can cache longer.
- Edge-level changes are reliably faster than DNS changes for most traffic.
- For tests, prefer:
  1) orchestrator change (policy-based)
  2) Cloudflare pool member weight/health override
  3) DNS-based switch only if edge control is impaired

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rollback plan (by change type)

1) Rollback: orchestrator-driven policy change (preferred)
- Action: set failover state machine back to “NORMAL”; remove scoped rule(s) for route/tier/model.
- Expected time: <2 minutes to stop shifting new traffic (edge config propagation).
- Verification:
  - traffic distribution returns to baseline (per-region QPS)
  - tail latency and 5xx stabilize within 10–15 min
  - capacity signals in both regions return to steady state

2) Rollback: Cloudflare origin pool member override (health/weight)
- Action: revert pool weights to baseline; remove “force unhealthy” markers.
- Expected time: ~1–3 minutes.
- Verification: same as above; plus check origin health checks show green across members.

3) Rollback: DNS TTL changes
- Action: restore TTL from 60s → 300s after the window.
- Expected time: immediate on authoritative; caches converge gradually but higher TTL is safe.

4) Rollback: DNS emergency switch (edge CNAME target)
- Action: revert CNAME to previous edge target.
- Expected time: unpredictable; depends on caching. This is why we keep this as last resort.
- Requirement: if we ever do this in prod, we open an incident and page Infra + SRE (treat as SEV2 at minimum).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Change windows + required sequencing

Staging (ENG-2850)
- Preferred window: Tue–Thu, 10:00–14:00 PT (lowest coordination overhead; enough coverage)
- Pre-reqs (T-2 days):
  - verify health checks from >=2 probe locations per region
  - set TTL to 60s for staging hostnames (Table A)
  - confirm capacity headroom in target region (Vanessa/Harish)
- Day-of:
  - freeze other edge/DNS changes during the window
  - record start/end times for later correlation (SLO toolkit)
- Post:
  - revert TTL to 300s
  - capture Cloudflare change log + orchestrator audit entries

Production low-risk slice (ENG-2851)
- Preferred window: Wed, 09:00–11:00 PT (paired with on-call coverage; avoids Fri)
- Approvals required in thread + change ticket:
  - Irene (Infra), Connor (Release), Rafael (SRE), Mina (Routing)
- Pre-reqs (T-5 to T-3 days):
  - lower TTL to 60s on prod edge hostnames (Table A) >=24h before window
  - confirm region pair and scope (e.g., only Hosted API free tier OR internal canary tenants)
  - ensure target region has N+1 capacity for expected shift + burst margin
  - confirm comms plan ready (Support macro + status page internal template)
- Hard stop conditions (infra-specific):
  - if Cloudflare health checks flap >3 times in 10 min (likely probe noise)
  - if packet loss on cross-region links exceeds threshold (Emily to provide)
  - if target region NLB 5xx increases beyond agreed baseline

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Records / identifiers to keep handy during game day (copy/paste)

Cloudflare
- Zone: redwoodinference.com
- DNS records:
  - api.redwoodinference.com → api-edge.prod.redwoodinfra.net
  - stream.redwoodinference.com → stream-edge.prod.redwoodinfra.net
- Origin pools:
  - api-prod pool id: (to fill)
  - stream-prod pool id: (to fill)
- Change log link: (to fill)

AWS / Route53
- Hosted zone: redwoodinfra.net (private) + redwoodinfra.net (public origins if applicable)
- Route53 change request template: (to fill)
- NLBs:
  - use1 api nlb: nlb-api-use1-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com
  - usw2 api nlb: nlb-api-usw2-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com
  - use1 stream nlb: nlb-stream-use1-prod-xxxx.elb.amazonaws.com
